detail:
BrainFacts.org, presenting the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) Diseases A–Z material, describes essential tremor as the most common form of abnormal tremor: an unintentional, somewhat rhythmic muscle movement involving to-and-fro oscillations of one or more parts of the body. The hands are most often affected, but symptoms can include tremor of the head, arms, voice, tongue, legs, and trunk, which can interfere with purposeful movements such as eating, writing, sewing, or shaving.

Onset is most common after age 40, although symptoms can appear at any age, and the source notes that children of a parent with essential tremor have up to a 50 percent chance of inheriting the condition. Heightened emotion, stress, fever, physical exhaustion, or low blood sugar may trigger tremors or increase their severity, and mild degeneration in parts of the cerebellum may be present. Essential tremor is not associated with any known pathology, and although it is not life-threatening, the source notes it can make daily tasks harder and can be embarrassing.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about essential tremor symptoms and diagnosis.
summary: BrainFacts.org, drawing on NINDS, describes essential tremor as the most common abnormal tremor, a rhythmic shaking most often of the hands that frequently runs in families and is not associated with any known pathology.
takeaways: essential tremor is the most common form of abnormal tremor
symptoms can include shaking of the hands, head, voice, and trunk
the condition often runs in families, per the source
title: Essential Tremor: the most common abnormal tremor
